result:
I fixed all 10 rules whose behavior didn't match their docstrings. I wrote a check script that reads each of the 150 rules' docstrings and compares the actual results against the docstring formula over many quantity and unit price combinations, including the values right around each threshold. Every rule now matches.

| Rule | Line | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 06 | `pricebook.py:64` | The discount started at 31 units, not 30 | `qty >= 30` |
| 25 | `pricebook.py:248` | It took 9% off instead of 8% | `* 8 // 100` |
| 43 | `pricebook.py:425` | `round()` broke the "floored to the won" rule | `base * 12 // 100` |
| 81 | `pricebook.py:798` | The 50,000 won cap only applied once the discount went over 100,000 won | `min(disc, 50000)` |
| 84 | `pricebook.py:827` | The 30,000 won cap only applied once the discount went over 60,000 won | `min(disc, 30000)` |
| 89 | `pricebook.py:876` | It took 16% off instead of 15% | `* 15 // 100` |
| 94 | `pricebook.py:925` | It took 16% off instead of 15% (marginal rule) | `* 15 // 100` |
| 95 | `pricebook.py:935` | `round()` broke the floor rule | `base * 8 // 100` |
| 106 | `pricebook.py:1043` | `round()` broke the floor rule | `base * 7 // 100` |
| 118 | `pricebook.py:1161` | The discount started at 13 units, not 12 | `qty >= 12` |

A few rules are written differently from the rest, such as `if not qty < N`, `if N <= qty`, or a marginal rule using `qty > N`. They give the same results as their docstrings, so I left them alone. (For example, a marginal rule's discount at exactly the threshold is 0 anyway.) Only the 10 rules above changed, and the original file is backed up at `/tmp/chk/pricebook.orig.py`.

STATUS: DONE
